chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Taking Monk and Bud to church
summary: Monk, Hal Baker and Bud Powell met her at Our Lady of Lourdes; Monk drank wine first and fell in the door.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I hope. Mary, once you went through this period of praying and being away from music and in the church, what was the reaction of the people aside from Dizzy that you knew in the jazz world, to what was happening?

Not immediately. I used to give prayers for musicians and Monk, Hal Baker, Bud Powell in the summer would meet me at the Lady of Lourdes. Mass went on at 6:30 then, I think, or 7. They'd meet me at 6 o'clock and they'd go in church with me. I'd keep them through three masses. The first time I took Monk to church, it wasn't during mass, it was in the afternoon. I said, 'Come on and meditate.' He told his wife, why don't you go with Mary? She said, 'Oh, go ahead, Monk,' so he finally made up his mind. He said, 'Why don't you go with her, Nelly?' Finally he made up his mind. He said, 'Wait a minute,' and I had a car and he stopped and went some place. I didn't watch where he had gone. He got himself a whole pint of wine or something and he drank all of it. So when we got to the church door Monk fell inside on the floor, fell out. I pulled him up and said, 'Get up, you big ape,' pulling on him and everything. See, during the afternoon there's nobody in church at all, you know, you can go and meditate. I said, 'What happened to you?' He wouldn't say anything and he sat down and he prayed and everything. But about a week later he said he thought he was going to die. (LAUGHTER)

The reason why he got the wine, he said he had never been in a church or anything like that before. He said he thought I was coming because I thought maybe he was going to die, so he went and got this wine and drank it. But I used to have a ball. I'd meet the musicians and like if anybody was hung up I'd take them into church and I'd teach them to pray, how to do the rosary beads. I used to sit in the Lady of Lourdes. I'd go to the mass in the morning, 7 o'clock mass, and sat through all the masses. I'd get out about 9 or 10. I'd come home and fix lunch for all the poor people I had in the house I was feeding. I'd go right back and meditate a couple hours and then I'd come home. I was from the house to the store to the church.
